objectives.text: Reiterate the AML program obligations on MSB principals to understand and appropriately account for the risks associated with their agents.

citations.quote: This guidance reiterates the anti-money laundering (AML) program obligations on the principals of money services businesses (MSBs)1 to understand and appropriately account for the risks associated with their agents,2 as broadly set forth by FinCEN in 2004 guidance primarily focused on foreign agents and counterparties.

objectives.text: Provide clarity so that MSB principals and their agents can more easily understand how to comply with AML requirements while providing important financial services.

citations.quote: This guidance is intended to provide clarity so that MSB principals and their agents can more easily understand how to comply with AML requirements while providing important financial services.

obligations.actor: all MSBs, both principals and their agents
obligations.action: establish and maintain an effective written AML program reasonably designed to prevent the MSB from being used to facilitate money laundering and the financing of terrorist activities

citations.quote: The Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) requires all MSBs, both principals and their agents, to establish and maintain an effective written AML program reasonably designed to prevent the MSB from being used to facilitate money laundering and the financing of terrorist activities.

obligations.action: remain independently and wholly responsible for implementing adequate AML program requirements; cannot avoid liability by pointing to a contract assigning this responsibility to another party

citations.quote: Moreover, each MSB remains independently and wholly responsible for implementing adequate AML program requirements.7 Accordingly, neither the agent nor the principal can avoid liability for failing to establish and maintain an effective AML program by pointing to a contract assigning this responsibility to another party (whether the agent or principal).

obligations.action: at a minimum: incorporate policies, procedures, and internal controls reasonably designed to assure compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations

citations.quote: Under 31 CFR § 1022.210, an MSB’s AML program must, at a minimum:
Incorporate policies, procedures, and internal controls reasonably designed to assure compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations

obligations.action: designate a person to assure day to day compliance with the program and the BSA and its implementing regulations

citations.quote: Designate a person to assure day to day compliance with the program and the BSA and its implementing regulations

obligations.action: provide education and training of appropriate personnel concerning their responsibilities under the program, including training in the detection of suspicious transactions to the extent that the MSB is required to report such transactions under the BSA

citations.quote: Provide education and training of appropriate personnel concerning their responsibilities under the program, including training in the detection of suspicious transactions to the extent that the money services business is required to report such transactions under the BSA

obligations.action: provide for independent review to monitor and maintain an adequate program

citations.quote: Provide for independent review to monitor and maintain an adequate program

obligations.action: have procedures in place to identify those agents conducting activities that appear to lack commercial purpose, lack justification, or otherwise are not supported by verifiable documentation
obligations.trigger: in order to reduce exposure to risks when an agent engages in transactions that create a risk for money laundering, terrorist financing, or other financial crime

citations.quote: the MSB principal must have procedures in place to identify those agents conducting activities that appear to lack commercial purpose, lack justification, or otherwise are not supported by verifiable documentation.

obligations.action: implement risk-based procedures to monitor the agents' transactions to ensure that they are legitimate

citations.quote: The principal must implement risk-based procedures to monitor the agents’ transactions to ensure that they are legitimate.

obligations.action: ensure that, if the agents' transactions trigger reporting or recordkeeping requirements, the principal handles the information in accordance with regulatory reporting and recordkeeping obligations
obligations.trigger: if the agents' transactions trigger reporting or recordkeeping requirements

citations.quote: The procedures must also ensure that, if the agents’ transactions trigger reporting or recordkeeping requirements, the principal handles the information in accordance with regulatory reporting and recordkeeping obligations.

obligations.action: implement procedures for handling non-compliant agents, including agent contract terminations

citations.quote: the MSB principal should implement procedures for handling non-compliant agents, including agent contract terminations.

obligations.action: develop and implement risk-based policies, procedures, and internal controls that ensure adequate ongoing monitoring of agent activity, as part of the principal's implementation of its AML program

citations.quote: principals are required to develop and implement risk-based policies, procedures, and internal controls that ensure adequate ongoing monitoring of agent activity, as part of the principal’s implementation of its AML program.

obligations.action: when conducting monitoring of their agents, at a minimum: identify the owners of the MSB's agents
obligations.trigger: when conducting monitoring of their agents

citations.quote: When conducting monitoring of their agents, principals must, at a minimum:
Identify the owners of the MSB’s agents

obligations.action: when conducting monitoring of their agents, evaluate on an ongoing basis the operations of agents, and monitor for variations in those operations
obligations.trigger: when conducting monitoring of their agents

citations.quote: Evaluate on an ongoing basis the operations of agents, and monitor for variations in those operations

obligations.action: when conducting monitoring of their agents, evaluate agents' implementation of policies, procedures, and controls
obligations.trigger: when conducting monitoring of their agents

citations.quote: Evaluate agents’ implementation of policies, procedures, and controls

obligations.action: periodically reassess risks associated with their agents and update the principals' programs to address any changing or additional related risks

citations.quote: Principals must periodically reassess risks associated with their agents and update the principals’ programs to address any changing or additional related risks.

obligations.action: take corrective action once becoming aware of any weaknesses or deficiencies in their AML programs
obligations.trigger: once becoming aware of any weaknesses or deficiencies in their AML programs

citations.quote: Principals must also take corrective action once becoming aware of any weaknesses or deficiencies in their AML programs.

obligations.action: conduct reviews with a scope and frequency commensurate with the risks of money laundering or other illicit activity such principal or agent faces
obligations.threshold: scope and frequency commensurate with the risks of money laundering or other illicit activity

citations.quote: MSB principals and agents are required to conduct reviews with a scope and frequency commensurate with the risks of money laundering or other illicit activity such principal or agent faces.

obligations.action: conduct internal and/or external independent testing to ensure there are no material weaknesses or internal control deficiencies; the testing must factor in products and services provided to determine if the procedures are sufficient to detect and report suspicious activity

citations.quote: A principal must conduct internal and/or external independent testing to ensure there are no material weaknesses (e.g., inadequate training) or internal control deficiencies (e.g., monitoring agents).
In addition, the testing must factor in products and services provided to determine if the procedures are sufficient to detect and report suspicious activity.

obligations.action: consider risk factors when conducting agent monitoring, including but not limited to whether owners are known or suspected associated with criminal conduct or terrorism, whether the agent has an established AML program, the nature of markets served, services expected and anticipated activity level, and the nature and duration of the relationship

citations.quote: Risk factors that principals should consider when conducting agent monitoring include, but are not limited to:
Whether the owners are known or suspected to be associated with criminal conduct or terrorism
The services an agent is expected to provide and the agent’s anticipated level of activity

obligations.actor: principals (with agents providing services involving regions affected by conflict or terrorism)
obligations.action: take steps to account for and mitigate such risks
obligations.trigger: agents providing services involving regions affected by conflict or terrorism

citations.quote: This does not mean that principals with agents providing services involving regions affected by conflict or terrorism cannot manage such risks, but rather that principals must take steps to account for and mitigate such risks

obligations.actor: MSB principals and agents (as expected by FinCEN)
obligations.action: tailor their AML programs to reflect the risks associated with their particular business services, clients, size, locations, and circumstances

citations.quote: FinCEN expects MSB principals and agents to tailor their AML programs to reflect the risks associated with their particular business services, clients, size, locations, and circumstances.

obligations.action: encouraged to share information with other eligible financial institutions through participation in the 314(b) voluntary information-sharing program where an agent has more than one principal or provides additional services on its own
obligations.trigger: an agent may enter into contracts to offer services with more than one principal or may provide additional services on its own

citations.quote: In such situations, principals are encouraged to share information with other eligible financial institutions through participation in the 314(b) voluntary information-sharing program.

definitions.definition: For purposes of this guidance includes authorized delegates, foreign agents or counterparties, agents and sub-agents.

citations.quote: The term “agent” for purposes of this guidance includes authorized delegates, foreign agents or counterparties, agents and sub-agents.

references: FinCEN Advisory on Promoting a Culture of Compliance (FIN-2014-A007, Aug. 11, 2014)

citations.quote: as has been highlighted in FinCEN’s Advisory to U.S. Financial Institutions on Promoting a Culture of Compliance.
The Advisory (Aug. 11, 2014) available at /system/files/shared/FIN-2014-A007.pdf.

interactions.description: FinCEN is working with its delegated examiner, the IRS Small Business/Self-Employed Division, and with state regulators to coordinate compliance and enforcement; expects a principal to have information readily available demonstrating effective risk-based monitoring of agent activity.
references: Internal Revenue Service's Small Business/Self-Employed Division

citations.quote: FinCEN is working closely with its delegated examiner, the Internal Revenue Service’s Small Business/Self-Employed Division, as well as with state regulators, to better coordinate compliance and enforcement efforts and maximize resources.

FinCEN expects a principal to have information readily available to demonstrate that it has effectively developed and implemented risk-based policies, procedures, and internal controls to ensure adequate ongoing monitoring of agent activity.

notes: This item is FinCEN agency guidance (FIN-2016-G001, evidence role agency_guidance) reiterating existing AML program-establishment/'pillars' obligations for MSB principals and agents — squarely within scope for MSBs under FinCEN. The document mixes binding modalities: it states program requirements are 'required'/'must' but also frames certain agent-monitoring elements with 'should' (e.g., handling non-compliant agents; risk factors principals 'should consider'), while stating FinCEN 'expects' tailoring — these expectation-framed duties are extracted at 'should' per the modality mapping since 'expects' is not a shall/must. Preserved as-written: OBL-17 uses 'are required to' (mapped must) for reviews, while OBL-18 uses 'must' for testing; the guidance also notes an internal ambiguity in that contractual allocation is permitted yet both parties 'remain liable' and 'each MSB remains independently and wholly responsible' (extracted verbatim, not harmonized). SAR/CTR/recordkeeping references (OBL-09) touch the coordination layer but are extracted only as stated in the program-establishment context. Depository Institutions is tagged on the page but the substantive obligations address MSB principals/agents only.
